# Set-ZbxMaintenance

## SYNOPSIS

Changes a maintenance period.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxMaintenance [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixMaintenanceRecord>[]> [[-Name] <string>] [-MaintenanceType <ZabbixMaintenanceDataCollectionType>] [-Description <string>] [-ActiveSince <DateTimeOffset>] [-ActiveTill <DateTimeOffset>] [-TagsEvaluationType <ZabbixEvaluationType>] [-Tag <ZabbixMaintenanceTagRequest[]>] [-Group <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHostGroup>[]>] [-HostReference <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHost>[]>] [-TimePeriod <ZabbixMaintenanceTimePeriodRequest[]>] [-Trigger <ZabbixReference<ZabbixTrigger>[]>] [-EventName <ZabbixMaintenanceEventNameRequest[]>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-PipedRecord <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A maintenance period suppresses problems, and optionally data collection, for hosts and host groups during planned work. The Set-ZbxMaintenance cmdlet changes the maintenance periods given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with maintenance.update; a field whose parameter is not given keeps its value. Every maintenance period the pipeline brings is changed in one call when the pipeline ends, and -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name. The command writes nothing unless -PassThru is given, which reads the changed maintenance periods back and writes them; -WhatIf shows what would change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Extend a maintenance by an hour

```powershell
$m = Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch window' -SelectTimePeriods
$period = New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Onetime -StartDate $m.ActiveSince -Period 7200
Set-ZbxMaintenance -InputObject 'Patch window' -ActiveTill ($m.ActiveSince + [TimeSpan]::FromHours(2)) -TimePeriod $period -PassThru |
    Select-Object Name, ActiveSince, ActiveTill
```

-InputObject takes a name, id or object; only the parameters given are sent (maintenance.update). With -PassThru the changed maintenance is read back and written to the pipeline.

### Example 2: Change the hosts a maintenance covers

```powershell
Set-ZbxMaintenance -InputObject 'Patch window' -Host 'web-01', 'db-01'
(Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch window' -SelectHosts).Hosts.HostName
```

-Host (the alias of -HostReference) and -Group replace the whole list, they do not add to it: include every host that should stay covered.

### Example 3: Update every maintenance a search finds, through the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch*' | Set-ZbxMaintenance -Description 'Approved in CHG-1042' -WhatIf
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch*' | Set-ZbxMaintenance -Description 'Approved in CHG-1042' -PassThru | Select-Object Name, Description
```

Get-ZbxMaintenance writes maintenance objects; Set-ZbxMaintenance binds each one. Run it with -WhatIf first.
